title: Add Graceful Shutdown with Signal Handling
description: Implements graceful shutdown for the yantraverse HTTP server, handling SIGTERM/SIGINT to stop accepting new requests, finish in‑flight requests, and run cleanup hooks. This reduces abrupt terminations, prevents data loss, and improves reliability in production environments.
testCases: Simulate SIGTERM while the server processes a long‑running request and verify the request completes before the process exits
Trigger SIGINT and ensure all registered cleanup callbacks are invoked exactly once and the server closes without errors
acceptance: When the process receives SIGTERM or SIGINT, the server stops accepting new connections, waits for all active requests to finish (with a configurable timeout), executes all registered cleanup functions, and exits with code 0. If the timeout expires, the process exits with code 1. All tests pass and no unhandled promise rejections occur.
reason: Production deployments need reliable termination to avoid dropped requests and resource leaks. Adding built‑in graceful shutdown aligns with the framework’s stability focus, eliminates the need for external scripts, and provides a ready‑to‑use pattern for users.
